review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–61) and compared it with the FDeriv version it wraps. The file has no @[simp] declarations and no simp-set interactions. Its lemmas are `eventually_left_inverse`, `eventually_right_inverse`, `map_nhds_eq`, `to_localInverse`, `to_local_left_inverse` and `isOpenMap_of_hasStrictDerivAt`. All of them are filter or HasStrictDerivAt statements with hypotheses that simp cannot discharge, so none is a sensible simp lemma. The FDeriv file has `@[simp] localInverse_apply_image`, which says `hf.localInverse f f' a (f a) = a`. The 1D `localInverse` is an `abbrev` for `(hf.hasStrictFDerivAt_equiv hf').localInverse _ _ _`. That makes it reducible, so simp may be able to reuse the FDeriv lemma. I did not confirm this, since I can't run Lean. I found no evidence of a missing canonical simp lemma, a wrongly oriented rule, competing rules or a rewrite cycle. A 1D `localInverse_apply_image` would be a mild nicety at most, so I am not reporting it.
